issues.description: Return-type mismatch for PersonService.getAllPersons: the problem statement and the template expect/getAllPersons to provide a list of Person objects (List<Person>), but the solution's PersonService implements getAllPersons returning a Set<Person>. This contradicts the specification (GET /persons should return a list) and the template method signature, and it also violates the problem note that PersonService attributes/signatures should not be changed. Students following the template and spec would implement and test against List<Person>, but the solution uses Set<Person>, creating confusion and potential compilation/type errors when integrating with code expecting a List.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep PersonService.getAllPersons signature and return type consistent with the template and problem statement: change the solution implementation to return List<Person> (e.g., return an unmodifiable List or new ArrayList with sorted elements). Implement the sorting on a List and return that List so the endpoint and client code expecting List<Person> remain compatible.

issues.description: Internal inconsistency in the solution: PersonResource.getAllPersons declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> but calls personService.getAllPersons(...) which in the solution returns Set<Person>. This mismatch (expecting a List but receiving a Set) will cause a type/error mismatch and prevents correct compilation/behavior of the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution internally consistent by ensuring PersonService.getAllPersons returns a List<Person> (matching PersonResource's ResponseEntity<List<Person>>). Alternatively, change PersonResource to return ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> and update the problem statement and client accordingly — but the preferred fix is to change PersonService to return List<Person> and adapt the sorting implementation to operate on and return a List.

issues.description: The contract for retrieving all persons is inconsistent across artifacts: the template PersonService defines getAllPersons(...) to return a List<Person>, the client and server REST layer expect/declare a List<Person> response, but the solution's PersonService returns a Set<Person>. This mismatch (List vs Set) for the same conceptual operation 'getAllPersons' creates mapping and integration confusion for students — they will see List-based APIs in the problem description, template stubs, and controllers, but find a different collection type in the provided solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent collection type for the getAllPersons contract across all artifacts. Prefer returning List<Person> from PersonService (matching the template, PersonResource response type, and client expectations). Update solution_repository/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java to return List<Person> (or change PersonResource and client to accept Set<Person>), and ensure all signatures and usages are aligned.
